clue.text: Secure with a coup de main?

definitions.text: Secure with a coup de main?

parts.words: Secure with a coup de main?
parts.note: a coup de main is a sudden attack, but read literally it is a blow of the hand: a cuff of the hand that restrains a prisoner

explanation.surface: A military raid that seizes its objective in one swift strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coup de main' looks like military jargon for a surprise attack; taken word by word it is 'stroke of the hand', and a cuff is a stroke, so a hand-cuff is how you secure someone.
explanation.definitionFit: These metal rings lock a prisoner's wrists, securing the person by the hands.

clue.text: Watch this horse

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on this particular horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged protective lid, and also a horse bred for riding to hounds.

clue.text: A number in excess

explanation.surface: A figure that is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old slang 'like ninety', meaning with great force or to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the figure nine times ten; and to go 'like ninety' is to go at it vigorously, to excess.

clue.text: Caesar's rugged beauty

parts.note: not a weather-beaten face: the queen was carried to Julius Caesar rolled up in a rug or bedding

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar's craggy good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Plutarch tells how the Egyptian queen was smuggled to Caesar wrapped in bedding; 'rugged' means rolled in a rug, not craggy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen was Julius Caesar's lover, famed for beauty, and delivered to him in a rug.

clue.text: Achieved by the winners in the Football Association's test paper

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, so FA's
taken as written
The Times is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: Winners' marks on a football exam paper set by the FA.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the governing body of English football; 'paper' is the newspaper The Times, in which this clue was printed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race the winners record the quickest results, the best clockings.

clue.text: South Africa's short but sound compositions

indicators.note: sound says the letters are to be spoken: S-A-S said out loud gives the word wanted

parts.note: SA is the short form of South Africa, so its possessive is SA's

explanation.surface: Short South African pieces of writing that are nonetheless solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like praise for the compositions, but it is the homophone signal: say the letters S, A, S one by one and you hear 'ess-ays'.
explanation.definitionFit: School essays are short written pieces, the commonest kind of literary composition.

clue.text: Good chap with a trick to make you jump

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated St
art can mean cunning or a trick

explanation.surface: A nice fellow with a prank to give you a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump suddenly in surprise or fright.

clue.text: Lithe cat is, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters of lithe cat are jumbled

explanation.surface: However you look at it, a supple cat is sporty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a lithe cat is sporty, and its letters, rearranged as 'anyhow' asks, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple, agile, strong animals are described as sporty and fit.

clue.text: "And creepy things with wings And gaunt and grisly" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: "And creepy things with wings And gaunt and grisly" (Gilbert)

parts.words: "And creepy things with wings And gaunt and grisly" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from W. S. Gilbert's ghost song in Ruddigore, naming the haunting apparitions

explanation.surface: A line of verse by Gilbert with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from the ghosts' scene in Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore; the missing plural noun is the ghosts themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt grisly apparitions are ghosts, the phantoms of the operetta's haunted picture gallery.

clue.text: A duck in five quarters? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in says the duck goes inside the string of compass points

parts.note: the quarters are compass points; here the run N, N, S, E, N, S, E
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A batsman out for nothing in five innings: what rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letters needed number seven (N, N, S, E, N, S, E), not five as printed; with O (a cricket duck) put inside after the first N, they spell the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations meaning that what was said is foolish talk.

clue.text: Lofty club

parts.note: not a high-class society but a golf iron with an angled face that sends the ball high

explanation.surface: An exclusive, superior social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofty' suggests snobbery; in golf to loft the ball is to hit it high, and this old iron (roughly a modern 5-iron) was made for that.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional golf iron, named for lofting the ball, is a kind of club.

clue.text: They may be the bell variety for certain belles

definitions.text: They may be the bell variety for certain belles

parts.words: They may be the bell variety for certain belles
parts.note: bell tents are cone-shaped tents; seaside ladies once changed in such shelters on the beach

explanation.surface: Bell-shaped items for certain pretty women.
explanation.walkthrough: A bell tent is a conical tent; the belles are bathers who changed in such tents on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Small changing shelters on beaches let swimmers change in privacy, often bell-shaped.

clue.text: Bar from the oldest opera

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words oldest opera, running across the word break

explanation.surface: Being banned from the most ancient opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'oldEST OPera'. To estop is a legal term for barring someone from asserting something.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, estoppel prevents or bars a party from going back on what it said before.

clue.text: Ten cat-men break the law

indicators.note: break says the letters of ten cat-men are to be broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of ten cat burglars breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like the gang's crime but is the anagram signal on TENCATMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by a legislature is a piece of law, an act.

clue.text: Wise precaution for an old man's side pain

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side after running
the old man is Father Time, so his pain lies in Time

explanation.surface: A sensible precaution when an elderly man suffers a pain in his side.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Father Time is the bearded figure of time personified, so a side pain belonging to him is a stitch in Time: the proverb 'a stitch in time saves nine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb praises a small repair made early that prevents bigger trouble, a sensible precaution.

clue.text: Make ordinary couple of girls go East

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name
Lis is a girl's name, short for Elisabeth

explanation.surface: A pair of young women heading east to become conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple of girls' gives two names, NORMA and LIS, then E for East is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring back to the usual, standard state.

clue.text: Doyle's band

parts.note: not a musical group: the title of a Sherlock Holmes story by Arthur Conan Doyle, about a spotted snake

explanation.surface: A pop group led by someone named Doyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adventure of the Speckled Band is a Holmes story whose 'band' turns out to be a deadly snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's story names the spotted snake 'the band', described by this word for spotted.

clue.text: Like one item of wedding wear

definitions.text: Like one item of wedding wear

parts.words: Like one item of wedding wear
parts.note: the bride wears something old, something new, something lent and something blue

explanation.surface: Describing something a bride puts on.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme says a bride should wear 'something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the bride's four customary items is lent by a friend, taken on loan.

clue.text: Nurses as first offenders?

explanation.surface: Trainee nurses taken for people convicted for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainee hospital nurses were called this in Britain; it also names criminals on probation, often first-time offenders spared prison.

clue.text: Boy meets doctor on the street? Not quite

indicators.note: on puts the doctor directly before the street in this down clue

parts.note: Al is a boy's name
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A lad meets a doctor out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and not quite both mean very close to but short of the full amount.

clue.text: In care for purpose

parts.note: to tend is to care for

explanation.surface: Being looked after for a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it as your purpose or aim.

clue.text: Portly body of Romans detailed to fast

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter of the Latin word goes

parts.note: corpus is the Latin, so the Romans', word for body
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A stout group of Romans assigned to go without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'assigned' but means de-tailed: the last S of CORPUS is removed before LENT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent and portly both describe a stout, heavy body.

clue.text: Treatment of American germanium

parts.note: USA stands for the United States of America
Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium

explanation.surface: How American germanium is processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means the way something is handled or treated.

clue.text: Gross style of wrestling

explanation.surface: A crude, unpleasant form of wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: A gross price is the inclusive one, everything counted; freestyle wrestling with few rules is also called by this name.

clue.text: Artful chap hides in the grass from the old magistrate

indicators.note: hides in says the artful chap is tucked inside the grass

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a man full of art

explanation.surface: A crafty fellow lurks in the long grass, hiding from the elderly judge.
explanation.walkthrough: An MA (Master of Arts) is taken as a man full of art; put MA inside LAWN. The answer is an old word for a magistrate in Viking and Danelaw England.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Danelaw, a lawman was an officer who declared the law, an early magistrate.

clue.text: The remedy for Cupid's dart?

parts.note: Cupid's dart makes people dote, so the cure is something set against doting

explanation.surface: Asking what cures being shot by the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ANTI-DOTE, the word reads 'against doting', the very cure for someone struck by love.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that counters a poison is a remedy; here it counters infatuation.

clue.text: City right for the artful

parts.note: Dodge City is the Kansas cow town of Wild West fame

explanation.surface: A city suited to crafty people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist, so 'the artful' points to his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's pickpocket is nicknamed the Artful Dodger, so the adjective calls up his name.

clue.text: Stated to be a lock returned to Edward

indicators.note: returned says the word for a lock of hair is turned round

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A lock of hair given back to a man called Edward, as declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like giving the hair back but turns TRESS into SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it firmly.
